Clinical Patient Care (Inpatient & Outpatient) Comprehensive Management: Provide expert diagnosis, treatment, and holistic care for adult patients presenting with complex, multi-system, or chronic medical conditions. Ward Rounds: Conduct regular consultant-led inpatient rounds to review treatment trajectories, evaluate clinical progress, and modify management plans. Outpatient Services: Run specialized medicine outpatient departments (OPD) for scheduled consultations, follow-up of chronic illnesses (e.g., hypertension, diabetes, chronic kidney disease), and preventative health screenings. Emergency & Critical Care: Oversee the management of acute medical emergencies (e.g., severe sepsis, acute respiratory failure, acute cardiac events, metabolic crises) and coordinate stabilization prior to any necessary higher-level tertiary transfers. 2. Diagnostic Stewardship & Procedural Skills Evidence-Based Investigations: Rationalize and interpret diagnostic workups, including laboratory panels, bedside point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS), imaging, and electrocardiography (ECG). Infectious Disease Surveillance: Maintain high clinical vigilance for regional and endemic infectious diseases prevalent in the Cox's Bazar region (e.g., vector-borne illnesses, acute enteric infections, drug-resistant pathogens) and ensure adherence to local antibiotic stewardship protocols. Duty Roster & Workflow: Supervise on-call rosters, hand-over protocols, and emergency response coordination to ensure 24/7 medical coverage continuity. Multidisciplinary Collaboration: Coordinate seamlessly with surgery, obstetrics/gynecology, pediatrics, and diagnostic departments to streamline holistic patient pathways. 4. Administrative & Public Health Responsibilities Clinical Audits & Protocols: Help formulate, update, and implement standard operating procedures (SOPs), clinical pathways, and infection control guidelines tailored to a secondary hospital setting. Public Health Integration: Participate in local health initiatives, outbreak responses, community health education, free medical camps and evidence-based clinical audits relevant to the local population. 5. company_business:
Gono Bishwabidyalay - a university with a difference- has been established to provide a high quality of education to meet the demands of the modern age. The objective of the Gono Bishwabidyalay is to foster the national and global development process through the creation of a centre of excellence in higher education that is responsive to society’s needs, particularly social development and human welfare. And to produce highly skilled manpower, visionary leaders and enlightened citizen by imparting high quality higher education and training so that individuals can achieve their intellectual, social, and personal potentials.
Gono Bishwabidyalay (GB) was established by Gonoshasthaya Kendra (GK) Public Charitable Trust that came into being during our glorious War of Liberation in 1971. It is noteworthy thatGonoshasthaya Kendra (People’s Health Centre), one of the pioneering NGOs in Bangladesh is well known all over the world. The GK’s role since 1972 in the development of women and reducing gender inequality has had far-reaching effect. Moreover, by bringing into effect a system of health insurance, protection of women’s right, preservation of folk culture and art, and by playing a leading role in the formulation of Bangladesh National Drug Policy, the GK has benefited the country in many ways. GK continually revisits its approaches to ensure its effectiveness as a catalyst for positive change. No wonder these services have been recognized by all concerned and GK was honored with many awards, such as – The Independence Day Award in 1978, Magsaysay Award in 1985 and in 1992 Right Livelihood Award from Swedish Parliament. With the same dedicated spirit and vision Gono Bishwabidyalay was established by GK on 14 July, 1998.
In line with GK’s continued support to education, the concept of Gono Bishwabidyalay was originated and established in 1994 in accordance with Bangladesh National Parliament Private University Act-1992. Gono Bishwabidyalay is a “not for profit” institution accredited by the University Grants Commission (UGC) and also approved by the Ministry of Education, Government of Bangladesh.
Most of the teachers of Gono Bishwabidyalay are full time, highly qualified, and well trained. It is worth mentioning, though the education provided by Gono Bishwabidyalay is of very high standard, its educational expenses are much less than that of other private universities in Bangladesh. It is, in fact, less than half and even within the reach of ordinary guardians. The education programmes of Gono Bishwabidyalay are semester based (six months). So the students can acquire standard education easily which is the case with universities in developed countries of the world.

job_description: Technical Qualities: Perform comprehensive psychological assessments using various diagnostic tools, interviews, and observation techniques to understand the needs, mental health, and emotional well-being of the survivors.
